# Results — Study 605 (VIX Settlement Day)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Griffin & Shams 2018, RFS — **"Manipulation in the VIX?"**) — VIX-derivative settlement
prints systematically deviate on the monthly settlement morning — asked of the daily index
tape: **does the settlement Wednesday leave tracks in ^VIX?** Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the
last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprints
`2f08bb9304e8` (^VIX) / `731fc130d08d` (^GSPC).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily ^VIX OHLC (5,659 rows) + ^GSPC OHLC (5,658 rows), 2004-01-02 → 2026-06-30 |
| Settlement calendar | built **by rule** (Wednesday 30 days before the following month's S&P-500 option expiry, holiday-adjusted) and asserted against **18 known CBOE dates**, incl. all **7 holiday-shifted Tuesdays** (2008-02-19, 2014-03-18, 2019-03-19, 2022-03-15, 2024-06-18, 2025-03-18, 2026-05-19) |
| Events | **270** monthly settlements on the tape vs **899** other Wednesdays; **40** settlements coincide with FOMC statement days (the Wednesday confounder — controlled below) |
| Statistics | Welch *t* for group splits; **White (HC1)** robust *t* for the regressions (non-overlapping single-day events — no overlapping-window serial correlation to Newey-West away) |
| Execution / costs | tradability rule has **one clean lag**: the calendar is known years ahead, the signal is the just-printed settlement-day *open* vs yesterday's close, entry at that open, exit at the close; costs **25 bps one-way × 2** per event at VIX-futures retail levels |
| Data quirk (named) | Yahoo ^VIX opens exactly equal the prior close on ~4% of days (~30% in 2008-09) — a stale-open artefact; the headline signature is re-run with those days dropped |

No survivorship: ^VIX and ^GSPC are indices, not a survivor panel.

## Level tests — the planned Welch splits (settlement days vs other Wednesdays)

| metric | settlement | other Wed | Welch *t* (all) | Welch *t* (**ex-FOMC**) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| open gap ln(O/C₋₁), mean | +0.043% | +0.016% | +0.11 | — |
| **\|open gap\|** | 2.410% | 2.185% | +1.30 | **+0.90** |
| intraday ln(C/O), mean | −0.238% | −0.762% | +1.06 | — |
| \|intraday\| | 5.000% | 4.468% | +1.48 | — |
| **\|close-close\|** | 5.861% | 4.880% | **+2.42** | **+1.73** |
| **range (H−L)/C₋₁** | 10.088% | 9.078% | **+2.17** | **+0.98** |
| **SPX close-close, mean** | −0.079% | +0.090% | **−2.06** | **−1.77** |

Two level effects clear *t* = 2 at first glance (settlement days look ~1 vol-point noisier,
SPX looks slightly red) — **and both die once FOMC statement days are removed** (40 of 270
settlements are also FOMC days; ex-FOMC n = 230 vs 797). The "louder day" story is mostly
the Fed, not the settlement. **No level test survives the confounder control.**

## The signature — settlement × gap **continuation** (the real track)

On a normal Wednesday the VIX morning gap *mean-reverts* into the close. If the settlement
auction pushes the morning print through the actual option book, the distorted open should
instead *carry into the day*. Regression on settlement days + other Wednesdays,
`intr = a + b·gap + c·sett + d·(gap × sett)`, White (HC1) *t*:

| sample | base slope *b* (other Wed) | settlement slope *b+d* | interaction *d* | *t(d)* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| all days (n = 1,169) | −0.179 (*t* = −2.30) | +0.249 | **+0.427** | **+2.56** |
| **ex-FOMC (n = 1,027)** | −0.195 (*t* = −2.42) | +0.302 | **+0.497** | **+2.86** |

The sign **flips**: other Wednesdays fade ~18-20% of the morning gap by the close; settlement
Wednesdays *extend* it by ~25-30%. Controlling FOMC makes the signature **stronger**, not
weaker.

**Random-calendar placebo** (one fake settlement Wednesday per month among non-settlement
Wednesdays, ex-FOMC, same regression): observed *d* = **+0.497** vs placebo mean **−0.023**
(sd 0.172) over **2,000 draws / 25 seeds** → two-sided **p = 0.0025**.

Robustness (ex-FOMC): dropping the Yahoo stale-open days leaves *d* = **+0.496**
(*t* = +2.86, n = 986); winsorising gap/intraday at 1%/99% leaves *d* = **+0.447**
(*t* = +2.81) — neither the data quirk nor the tails carry it.

## Third axis — did it fade after Griffin-Shams (2018) + the manipulation lawsuits?

| quantity | 2004-2017 | 2018-2026 |
|---|--:|--:|
| continuation interaction *d* (ex-FOMC) | **+0.468** (*t* = +2.31, n_sett = 148) | **+0.490** (*t* = +1.53, n_sett = 82) |
| \|close-close\| level effect, Welch *t* (with FOMC) | **+3.10** | +0.18 |
| \|close-close\| level effect, Welch *t* (ex-FOMC) | **+2.21** | −0.20 |

A genuinely **mixed** fade: the *extra-volatility level effect* that existed pre-2018
disappeared entirely — but the **continuation signature did not fade at all** in point
estimate (+0.468 → +0.490); it merely loses stand-alone significance on the smaller
post-2018 sample (82 settlements, *t* = 1.53). The paper and the lawsuits did not visibly
kill the mechanism the paper described.

## Tradability arithmetic — the honest cash-out attempt

The only sign-tradable expression of the signature: at the settlement-day open, ride the gap
direction to the close (position = sign(gap); one clean lag — calendar known years ahead,
signal is the just-printed open). In **index log units** (the VIX index is **not tradable**):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| settlement days, gross/event | **−0.024%** (*t* vs 0 = −0.05, *t* vs other Wed = +0.67, n = 262) |
| other Wednesdays, gross/event | −0.361% |
| net of 2 × 25 bps/event | **−0.524%** /event × 12 events/yr = **−6.29%/yr** of notional |

The signature is an OLS moment (magnitude-weighted), not a sign edge: the paper value of the
tradable rule is **zero before costs** and deeply negative after — and even that ignores the
futures-vs-spot basis (VIX futures under-react to spot morning moves) and that the *expiring*
contract has already printed its SOQ by the time the signal exists. Nothing here is
deployable. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful

A deterministic 44-year world (seed 605) where normal-day gaps mean-revert (slope −0.20) and
settlement days carry a **planted** extra gap→close slope:

| planted *d* | recovered *d* | *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| **0.00 (null)** | +0.025 | **+0.25** |
| **+0.50** | +0.525 | **+5.22** |

The null stays quiet, the planted signature is recovered without bias. *(Machinery proof
only — never cited in support of the Signal stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — MIXED.** *Real on the structure, none on the level.* The settlement-morning
  **continuation signature** clears the bar on the real tape: interaction **+0.427**
  (White *t* = **+2.56**) on all days, **+0.497** (*t* = **+2.86**) ex-FOMC, random-calendar
  placebo **p = 0.0025**, robust to the stale-open screen and to winsorising. But every
  **level** test the plan pre-registered (open jump, day volatility, range, SPX drift) dies
  once the 40 settlement-FOMC overlap days are controlled (all ex-FOMC *t* < 2). The
  settlement Wednesday leaves a track — just not the loud one.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The VIX index is not tradable; the sign-rule paper value is
  −0.024%/event gross (t ≈ 0) and −6.3%/yr net of futures-level costs; 12 events/yr, the
  expiring contract has already settled when the signal prints, and the futures basis eats
  the rest.
- **"Did it fade after the 2018 paper + lawsuits?" — MIXED.** The extra-volatility level
  effect vanished (|Δclose| Welch *t* +3.10 → +0.18) — but the continuation signature's
  point estimate did not budge (+0.468 → +0.490, under-powered *t* = 1.53 on 82
  post-2018 settlements).
